title: CFE® Credential (Certified Fraud Examiner)
source: ACFE Fraud Examiners Manual & CFE Candidate Handbook
summary: The global gold standard in fraud examination, forensic accounting, white-collar criminology, and anti-fraud deterrence, evaluated across 4 comprehensive examination sections and a 50-point qualification system.

standard.name: Standard CFE Track
standard.blurb: Achieve 50 qualification points, pass all 4 computer-based examination sections (75% passing score each), and document 2 years of fraud-related experience.

stages.title: Stage 1: Eligibility & 50-Point Qualification System
stages.subtitle: ACFE membership and points-based academic/experience evaluation

nodes.name: Join ACFE & Establish Candidate Profile
nodes.description: Maintain active Associate membership in the ACFE and open an official CFE candidate profile.

nodes.name: Earn 50 Qualification Points
nodes.description: Accumulate 50 qualification points based on education (Bachelor's degree = 40 points) and professional experience (1 year = 5 points). Minimum 40 points required to sit for the exam.
topics: 40 Points for Bachelor's Degree
5 Points per Year of Fraud Experience
Point System Thresholds

stages.title: Stage 2: Sections 1 & 2 Examinations
stages.subtitle: Financial Transactions & Fraud Schemes, and Law

nodes.name: Section 1: Financial Transactions & Fraud Schemes
nodes.description: Basic accounting theory, internal control vulnerabilities, asset misappropriation (skimming, larceny, billing, payroll, check tampering), corruption, and financial statement fraud schemes.
topics: Basic Accounting Theory & Internal Controls
Asset Misappropriation: Cash Receipts & Fraudulent Disbursements
Corruption: Bribery, Kickbacks, Bid-Rigging & Conflicts of Interest
Financial Statement Fraud: Fictitious Revenues, Timing Differences, Concealed Liabilities
Specialized Schemes: Healthcare, Insurance, Securities & Consumer Fraud

nodes.name: Section 2: Law
nodes.description: Criminal and civil justice systems, rules of evidence, courtroom testimony, legal rights of suspects during interviews, search and seizure, and privacy laws.
topics: Civil vs Criminal Legal Systems & Burdens of Proof
Rules of Evidence, Chain of Custody & Document Authenticity
Suspect Rights, Search and Seizure, and Self-Incrimination Protections
Expert Witness Testimony & Federal Rules of Evidence

nodes.name: Section 3: Investigation
nodes.description: Forensic interviewing techniques, deception detection, digital evidence collection, public records searches, tracing illicit assets, and formal fraud investigation reporting.
topics: Forensic Interviewing Techniques & Admission-Seeking Interviews
Digital Forensics, E-Discovery & Metadata Preservation
Tracing Illicit Assets & Net Worth Analysis Methodologies
Writing Comprehensive Fraud Investigation Reports

nodes.name: Section 4: Fraud Prevention & Deterrence
nodes.description: White-collar criminological theories (Fraud Triangle, Cressey, Hollinger-Clark), fraud risk assessment, COSO internal controls, anti-fraud governance, and whistleblower hotlines.
topics: Criminological Theories of White-Collar Crime & Fraud Triangle
Developing Organizational Anti-Fraud Policies & Ethics Programs
Fraud Risk Assessment Methodologies & COSO Controls Integration
Whistleblower Protection, Hotline Management & Fraud Prevention Culture

stages.title: Stage 4: Professional Experience & Credential Award
stages.subtitle: 2 Years Verified Fraud Experience + Annual CPE

nodes.name: 2 Years Qualifying Fraud-Related Experience
nodes.description: Demonstrate at least 2 years of professional experience in fraud examination, forensic accounting, financial auditing, criminology, loss prevention, or legal investigation.
topics: 24 Months Qualifying Experience
Supervisory Professional Verification

nodes.name: Certified Fraud Examiner Designation Conferred
nodes.description: Formal conferral of the CFE credential upon passing all 4 exam sections and achieving 50 total qualification points. Requires 20 hours annual CPE (2 hours in ethics).
topics: CFE Credential Award
20 Hours Annual CPE
2 Hours Ethics CPE
Active ACFE Membership
